encounters.cc: Left knee pain and difficulty walking with gradual bowing of the left leg

lines: Left knee pain and difficulty walking with gradual bowing of the left leg
He presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of increasing left knee pain and difficulty walking.
He reports a gradual bowing of his left leg.
He also mentions occasional headaches and a recent difficulty in hearing, especially in noisy environments.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
His medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
On physical examination, there is noticeable frontal bossing and warmth over the left tibia, which is tender to palpation.
There is also a palpable enlargement of the tibia compared to the right.
Knee examination reveals crepitus with movement and tenderness on the medial side.

encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty swallowing solids and liquids with 15-pound weight loss

lines: Progressive difficulty swallowing solids and liquids with 15-pound weight loss
He returns following rheumatology care for Paget disease.
He reports a 15-pound weight loss during this period.
He denies any history of heartburn or regurgitation.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
His past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
On physical examination, he appears cachectic.
His abdomen is soft and non-tender, without any palpable masses.
- Liver function tests: Within normal limits
A barium swallow study shows a dilated esophagus with a "bird's beak" appearance at the distal end.

encounters.cc: Palpitations and intermittent shortness of breath for two weeks

lines: Palpitations and intermittent shortness of breath for two weeks
The patient returns after rheumatology and gastroenterology visits with palpitations and intermittent shortness of breath for the past two weeks and denies chest pain, dizziness, or syncope.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
His current medications include hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
His blood pressure is 158/92 mmHg, heart rate is irregularly irregular at 110 bpm, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
On auscultation, there are no crackles or wheezes, and the remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows no evidence of ischemia but confirms atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of approximately 110 bpm.

encounters.cc: Follow-up after left leg DVT diagnosed three weeks ago following transatlantic flight

lines: Follow-up after left leg DVT diagnosed three weeks ago following transatlantic flight

The patient is a 70-year-old male with valvular atrial fibrillation secondary to rheumatic heart disease, Paget disease of bone, and achalasia who returns for follow-up of his left leg deep vein thrombosis.
His symptoms began after a transatlantic flight, and he was started on oral rivaroxaban at the time of diagnosis.
He reports that swelling and discomfort have improved significantly.
He states he appreciates not having to undergo frequent blood tests or make dietary changes.
He also inquires whether a recent course of antibiotics for sinusitis could interfere with his treatment.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
His medical history includes hypertension and osteoarthritis.
He takes he takes lisinopril and ibuprofen.
His brother who takes a different medication for atrial fibrillation and was told to avoid leafy greens and watch his antibiotic use
He denies new leg pain, shortness of breath, or bleeding
Physical exam shows mild residual edema in the left leg

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset right arm weakness and slurred speech beginning two hours ago

lines: Sudden-onset right arm weakness and slurred speech beginning two hours ago
This 71-year-old male with valvular atrial fibrillation and prior DVT is brought to the emergency department due to sudden-onset right arm weakness and slurred speech that began 2 hours ago.
He has not seen a physician in many years.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
Recalls having rheumatic fever as a child.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
His BP is 115/75 and HR is 90.
Neurologic exam shows right-sided facial droop and 3/5 motor strength in the right upper extremity.
A low-pitched diastolic murmur is auscultated best at the apex.
Carotid ultrasound shows no significant stenosis.
A non-contrast head CT shows no hemorrhage.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset, severe diffuse abdominal pain with nausea for three hours

lines: Sudden-onset, severe diffuse abdominal pain with nausea for three hours
This 71-year-old with valvular atrial fibrillation presents with diffuse abdominal pain, 10/10 in intensity, and associated with nausea.
He denies vomiting, diarrhea, or fever.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
Blood pressure 145/90 mmHg, heart rate 110 bpm irregularly irregular, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, and temperature 98.6°F (37°C)
Soft abdomen with severe diffuse tenderness to palpation, but no rebound or guarding.
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.28, pCO2 28 mmHg, pO2 98 mmHg
An electrocardiogram confirms atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe pain with pallor and coldness in left lower extremity

lines: Sudden onset of severe pain with pallor and coldness in left lower extremity
This patient with valvular atrial fibrillation and prior mesenteric ischemia presents reporting the leg became pale and cold approximately 2 hours ago.
He denies any trauma or prior similar episodes.
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
His medications include warfarin and metoprolol.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
On examination, the left lower extremity is cold to touch, with absent pulses distal to the femoral artery.
There is no sensory loss or motor weakness, and the right lower extremity is normal.
The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.
His laboratory values are as follows:
An urgent Doppler ultrasound of the left lower extremity shows no flow in the popliteal artery.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset weakness of right arm and face with inability to grip objects

lines: Sudden-onset weakness of right arm and face with inability to grip objects

The patient with valvular atrial fibrillation on rivaroxaban and prior thromboembolic events including right arm weakness in 2022 and mesenteric ischemia is unable to grip objects with his right hand, cannot raise his right eyebrow, and has drooping of the right corner of his mouth.
His right leg strength is preserved, and he has no sensory loss or visual changes.
- Acute arterial embolism of left lower extremity causing acute limb ischemia (diagnosed 2023-09-15)
- Atrial fibrillation (valvular, secondary to rheumatic heart disease)
Medical history includes hypertension and atrial fibrillation.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knee pain
He is alert and oriented, with intact language and cognitive function.
A non-contrast head CT confirms the diagnosis.
